title: Langtang Valley vs Gosaikunda Trek: Which to Choose
meta_description: Langtang Valley vs Gosaikunda trek compared: days, altitude, difficulty, views, crowds, season and cost, plus when to combine both in 11 days.
summary: Choose the Langtang Valley trek (7–8 days, Kyanjin Ri 4,773 m) for glaciers, yak pastures and close views of Langtang Lirung. Choose Gosaikunda (5–7 days, 4,380 m) for sacred lakes, pilgrimage and wide views west to Manaslu. With 11 days, combine them: acclimatising in the valley first makes Gosaikunda safer.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: The Langtang Valley and Gosaikunda lie on opposite sides of the Trishuli valley, both inside Langtang National Park and both reached by road from Kathmandu in a day. They are often confused, but they are different treks. The Langtang Valley trek follows the Langtang Khola from Syabrubesi to Kyanjin Gompa, a glacial basin below Langtang Lirung (7,227 m). The Gosaikunda trek climbs from Dhunche along a forested ridge to a chain of sacred alpine lakes at 4,380 m.

If you want big mountains close up and a gentler gradient, choose the Langtang Valley. If you are a pilgrim, want a lake and a wide panorama, or are coming for Janai Purnima, choose Gosaikunda. If you have 11 days or more and good fitness, do both: the trails connect through Thulo Syabru and Chandanbari, and the combination is one of the best moderate-length treks in Nepal.

sections.heading: Scenery and what you will see
paras: The Langtang Valley is a classic Himalayan valley walk. The first day and a half is in deep forest of oak, rhododendron and bamboo along a roaring river, home to langur monkeys and red pandas. Above Ghoda Tabela the valley opens into yak pastures with Langtang Lirung towering overhead, and at Kyanjin Gompa you are surrounded by glaciers and peaks on three sides. Kyanjin Ri gives a close, dramatic panorama, and the rebuilt village of Langtang adds a sobering human story from 2015.

Gosaikunda is about ridges and lakes. The walk from Dhunche climbs steeply through forest to Chandanbari and then onto an open ridge at Lauribina, where the view swings west to the Ganesh Himal, Manaslu and on clear days the Annapurnas. The lakes themselves sit in a stark, rocky basin, with Gosaikunda's small Shiva shrine on the shore. The views are wider and more distant than in the Langtang Valley, and the atmosphere is spiritual rather than pastoral.

sections.heading: Difficulty and altitude
paras: The Langtang Valley climbs gradually: about 1,000 m on day one, 960 m on day two and 440 m on day three, with a rest day at Kyanjin before climbing Kyanjin Ri. That gentle profile is why first-time trekkers do well here. Gosaikunda is steeper and faster. From Dhunche at 1,960 m to Chandanbari at 3,330 m is about 1,370 m of ascent in one day, and the next day adds another 1,050 m to the lake. Sleeping at 4,380 m after only two days of walking is a big jump.

That is the main reason we recommend combining the two in the right order. Trekkers who spend three or four days in the Langtang Valley and climb Kyanjin Ri arrive at Gosaikunda already acclimatised, and the climb feels much easier. If you do Gosaikunda alone, add a night at Lauribina (3,910 m) before the lake.

sections.heading: Crowds, culture and pilgrims
paras: Both treks are far quieter than Everest or Annapurna, but in different ways. The Langtang Valley sees a steady stream of international trekkers in October and April, staying in comfortable rebuilt lodges run by Tamang families. Gosaikunda is quiet most of the year, then fills with thousands of Hindu and Buddhist pilgrims around Janai Purnima in August, when lodges overflow and the trail becomes a procession.

Culturally, the Langtang Valley offers Tamang villages, mani walls, water-driven prayer wheels and the monastery at Kyanjin. Gosaikunda offers a living pilgrimage: puja at the shrine, holy dips, sacred threads and, at the festival, jhankri shamans drumming through the night. Indian pilgrims often choose Gosaikunda for this reason.
list: Choose Langtang Valley for glaciers, yak pastures and a gentle first trek
Choose Gosaikunda for pilgrimage, sacred lakes and the Janai Purnima festival
Choose both if you have 11 days and want the most variety for your effort
Add Helambu over Lauribina La for a 14-day traverse ending near Kathmandu

sections.heading: Best season for each
paras: Both treks are at their best from late September to November and from March to May. The Langtang Valley stays walkable in winter, with cold but clear days at Kyanjin, though snow can fall. Gosaikunda in winter is harder: the trail above Chandanbari is often snowbound, the lake freezes and Lauribina La towards Helambu can close from December to March. In the monsoon, from June to September, both are wet, but Gosaikunda has its festival in August, which draws pilgrims regardless of rain.

sections.heading: Sample itineraries compared
paras: Seeing the routes side by side helps. All three start and finish in Kathmandu and use a private jeep for the road sections. The combined trek uses the Langtang Valley first for acclimatisation, then crosses to Gosaikunda through Thulo Syabru and Chandanbari, finishing in Dhunche. If you have three more days, you can continue over Lauribina La to Helambu instead of descending to Dhunche.
list: Langtang Valley, 8 days: Syabrubesi, Lama Hotel, Langtang village, Kyanjin Gompa (2 nights with Kyanjin Ri), Lama Hotel, Syabrubesi, Kathmandu
Gosaikunda, 7 days: Dhunche, Chandanbari, Lauribina, Gosaikunda, Chandanbari, Dhunche, Kathmandu
Combined, 11 days: Syabrubesi, Lama Hotel, Langtang village, Kyanjin Gompa (2 nights), Lama Hotel, Thulo Syabru, Chandanbari, Gosaikunda, Dhunche, Kathmandu
Full traverse, 14 days: as combined, then Lauribina La, Ghopte, Melamchi Gaun, Tarkeghyang and a jeep to Kathmandu

sections.heading: Cost and logistics
paras: Costs are similar per day. A guided Langtang Valley trek of 8 days starts at about US$ 690 or ₹58,000 with us, a Gosaikunda pilgrimage of 7 days at about ₹36,000 on a group departure, and the 11-day combination at about US$ 890 or ₹75,000. Both use the same permits, the Langtang National Park entry fee and a TIMS card, plus a licensed guide for foreign trekkers. Transport is by jeep or bus from Kathmandu, with the Langtang trek starting in Syabrubesi and Gosaikunda in Dhunche, an hour apart on the same road.

For travellers short on time or unable to walk long days, both areas have helicopter options. A Langtang heli tour lands at Kyanjin Gompa for breakfast, and a Gosaikunda heli yatra lands beside the lake for darshan. Each takes about three hours from Kathmandu, weather permitting.

faqs.q: Is Gosaikunda harder than Langtang Valley?
faqs.a: Yes, generally. Gosaikunda gains height faster: about 2,400 m in two walking days from Dhunche to 4,380 m, on steep stone steps. The Langtang Valley climbs more gradually over three days to 3,870 m, with Kyanjin Ri as an optional high point. Doing Langtang first makes Gosaikunda easier.

faqs.q: Can I combine Langtang Valley and Gosaikunda?
faqs.a: Yes. After Kyanjin Gompa, walk down to Lama Hotel, cross to Thulo Syabru, climb to Chandanbari and then Gosaikunda, finishing in Dhunche. It takes about 11 days from Kathmandu. Our 11-day Langtang Gosaikunda trek follows this route, starting at US$ 890 per person.

faqs.q: Which has better mountain views, Langtang or Gosaikunda?
faqs.a: Langtang Valley gives close views of Langtang Lirung (7,227 m) and its glaciers, especially from Kyanjin Ri. Gosaikunda gives wider, more distant views from Lauribina, west to Ganesh Himal, Manaslu and the Annapurnas. For drama up close choose Langtang; for a broad panorama choose Gosaikunda.

faqs.q: Which trek is better for beginners?
faqs.a: The Langtang Valley trek is better for most beginners. Its height gain is gradual, lodges are frequent and comfortable, and a rest day at Kyanjin helps acclimatisation. Gosaikunda is steeper and reaches 4,380 m quickly. Beginners who want Gosaikunda should add an acclimatisation night at Lauribina.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Langtang and Gosaikunda?
faqs.a: Allow 7–8 days for the Langtang Valley alone, 5–7 days for Gosaikunda alone, and about 11 days for both together. Add three days if you want to continue over Lauribina La to Helambu, making a 14-day traverse that ends with a jeep or walk back to Kathmandu.

faqs.q: Do I need separate permits for Langtang and Gosaikunda?
faqs.a: No. Both are inside Langtang National Park, so one park entry permit and one TIMS card cover the whole route, including the combined trek. Foreign trekkers also need a licensed guide. Check current status before you travel, as rules and fees change.

faqs.q: Is Gosaikunda worth it without the festival?
faqs.a: Yes. Outside Janai Purnima, Gosaikunda is quiet and peaceful, with clear views in autumn and spring and a chance to take the holy dip without crowds. Many trekkers and pilgrims prefer October or May for this reason. The festival is remarkable but very crowded and falls in the monsoon.

The Langtang Valley has more and better lodges, many rebuilt after 2015, with attached bathrooms at Kyanjin Gompa. Gosaikunda's lake-side lodges are basic, with dormitories and outside toilets, and are packed during the festival. Chandanbari and Lauribina have simple but adequate lodges.

faqs.q: Can I do Gosaikunda by helicopter and Langtang on foot?
faqs.a: Yes. Some travellers trek the Langtang Valley and then take a short Gosaikunda helicopter yatra from Kathmandu, or add a Gosaikunda landing to a heli return from Kyanjin, weather permitting. This suits pilgrims in a group where not everyone can walk to the lake.
